name: 600 everyday chunks
description: 600 chunks with 1,200 sentence examples, 60 speaking prompts and an optional 180-session practice plan.

items.title: Nice to meet you.
items.cue: Greet someone for the first time.
items.model: It's nice to meet you, Daniel.
examples: It's nice to meet you at last.
items.meaning: Greet someone for the first time.
items.note: First meeting; use see you again for someone you know.

items.title: Nice to see you again.
items.cue: Greet someone you have met before.
items.model: It's nice to see you again, Mei.
examples: It's nice to see you again after so long.
items.meaning: Greet someone you have met before.

items.title: How have you been?
items.cue: Ask about life since your last meeting.
items.model: How have you been since we last spoke?
examples: How have you been these past few weeks?
items.meaning: Ask about life since your last meeting.

items.title: How's your day going?
items.cue: Ask about someone's day so far.
items.model: How's your day going so far, Anna?
examples: How's your day going at the new office?
items.meaning: Ask about someone's day so far.

items.title: I'm originally from [place].
items.model: I'm originally from Penang, but I live in KL.
examples: I'm originally from a small town near Ipoh.

items.title: I live in [place].
items.model: I live in an apartment near the station.
examples: I live in Johor Bahru with my family.

items.title: I work as [job].
items.model: I work as a designer for a small company.
examples: I work as an assistant in a local shop.
items.note: Use a/an before a singular job title.

items.title: I work in [field].
items.cue: Give your industry or work area.
items.model: I work in customer service.
examples: I work in education, mainly with adults.
items.meaning: Give your industry or work area.

items.title: You can call me [name].
items.model: You can call me Jay.
examples: You can call me Sam if that's easier.

items.title: I don't think we've met.
items.model: I don't think we've met; I'm Lina.
examples: I don't think we've met before this class.

items.title: I've heard a lot about you.
items.cue: Say someone has mentioned this person.
items.model: I've heard a lot about you from Amir.
examples: I've heard a lot about you and your cooking.
expressions: I've heard a lot about you.
items.meaning: Say someone has mentioned this person.
items.note: Use only when true.

items.title: Let me introduce you to [person].
items.model: Let me introduce you to my colleague, Ben.
examples: Let me introduce you to our new neighbour.

items.title: How do you know [person]?
items.model: How do you know the host?
examples: How do you know Sarah from the photography club?

items.title: Is this your first time here?
items.cue: Ask whether a place is new to someone.
items.model: Is this your first time here at the centre?
examples: Is this your first time here in Malaysia?
expressions: Is this your first time here?
items.meaning: Ask whether a place is new to someone.

items.title: I've just moved to [place].
items.model: I've just moved to this neighbourhood.
examples: I've just moved to a flat near my office.

items.title: I've been here for [time].
items.cue: Say how long you have stayed.
items.model: I've been here for about six months.
examples: I've been here for two hours already.
items.meaning: Say how long you have stayed.
items.note: Use for with a duration; since with a starting point.

items.title: I'm here for [reason].
items.cue: Explain the purpose of your visit.
items.model: I'm here for the English workshop.
examples: I'm here for a job interview.
items.meaning: Explain the purpose of your visit.

items.title: What brings you here?
items.model: What brings you here this afternoon?
examples: What brings you here to our community centre?

items.title: Please make yourself at home.
items.model: Please make yourself at home while I make tea.
examples: Please make yourself at home in the living room.

items.title: It's good to put a face to the name.
items.cue: Enjoy meeting someone previously known by name.
items.model: It's good to put a face to the name after our emails.
examples: It's good to put a face to the name at last.
expressions: It's good to put a face to the name.
items.meaning: Enjoy meeting someone previously known by name.
items.note: Friendly; common after email or phone contact.

items.title: How was your weekend?
items.model: How was your weekend with your family?
examples: How was your weekend in Melaka?

items.title: What have you been up to?
items.model: What have you been up to lately?
examples: What have you been up to since the course ended?
expressions: What have you been up to?
items.note: Friendly and conversational.

items.title: How's work?
items.cue: Ask how someone's working life is going.
items.model: How's work at the new company?
examples: How's work been this week?
items.meaning: Ask how someone's working life is going.

items.title: How's your family?
items.model: How's your family doing these days?
examples: How's your family settling into the new house?

items.title: How did [event] go?
items.cue: Ask about the result of an event.
items.model: How did your interview go yesterday?
examples: How did the driving lesson go?
items.meaning: Ask about the result of an event.

items.title: What do you do in your free time?
items.model: What do you do in your free time after work?
examples: What do you do in your free time at weekends?
expressions: What do you do in your free time?

items.title: What got you into [activity]?
items.model: What got you into photography?
examples: What got you into running in the first place?
items.note: Use a noun or -ing activity after into.

items.title: How long have you been [verb-ing]?
items.cue: Ask when an ongoing activity began.
items.model: How long have you been learning English?
examples: How long have you been working here?
items.meaning: Ask when an ongoing activity began.

items.title: What do you like most about [thing]?
items.model: What do you like most about your new job?
examples: What do you like most about living here?
expressions: What do you like most about [thing]?

items.title: Have you tried [thing]?
items.model: Have you tried the bakery across the street?
examples: Have you tried taking the train to work?

items.title: What's [thing] like?
items.model: What's your new neighbourhood like?
examples: What's the food like at that restaurant?
items.note: Different from What does it look like?, which asks about appearance.

items.title: Would you recommend it?
items.cue: Ask whether something is worth trying.
items.model: Would you recommend it to someone travelling alone?
examples: Would you recommend it for a family dinner?
items.meaning: Ask whether something is worth trying.

items.title: What happened next?
items.cue: Invite someone to continue a story.
items.model: What happened next after you missed the bus?
examples: What happened next when the lights went out?
items.meaning: Invite someone to continue a story.

items.title: How did you feel about it?
items.model: How did you feel about it when you heard?
examples: How did you feel about it afterwards?
expressions: How did you feel about it?

items.title: That reminds me of [thing].
items.cue: Connect a topic to your own experience.
items.model: That reminds me of my first day at work.
examples: That reminds me of a café we visited last year.
items.meaning: Connect a topic to your own experience.

items.title: Speaking of [topic], ...
items.model: Speaking of food, have you had lunch?
examples: Speaking of weekends, are you free on Sunday?

items.title: By the way, ...
items.model: By the way, I found your umbrella.
examples: By the way, the shop closes early today.

items.title: Do you come here often?
items.cue: Ask about someone's connection to a place.
items.model: Do you come here often for lunch?
examples: Do you come here often to study?
items.meaning: Ask about someone's connection to a place.
items.note: Tone and context matter; can sound like a social approach.

items.title: It's quite busy here today.
items.model: It's quite busy here today compared with yesterday.
examples: It's quite busy here today, so we may have to wait.

items.title: I love your [item].
items.model: I love your jacket; the colour really suits you.
examples: I love your bag; where did you get it?
items.note: Comment on chosen items rather than someone's body.

items.title: That makes sense.
items.model: That makes sense because the station is closer.
examples: That makes sense now that you've explained it.
items.note: Shows understanding; not always agreement or emotional comfort.

items.title: I see what you mean.
items.cue: Show that you understand a point.
items.model: I see what you mean about the price.
examples: I see what you mean now that I've tried it.
items.meaning: Show that you understand a point.

items.title: That sounds good.
items.model: That sounds good, so let's book a table.
examples: That sounds good to me for Saturday.

items.title: I'm glad to hear that.
items.model: I'm glad to hear that your trip went well.
examples: I'm glad to hear that you're feeling better.

items.title: I'm sorry to hear that.
items.model: I'm sorry to hear that you lost your bag.
examples: I'm sorry to hear that your week has been difficult.
items.note: Sympathy; it does not mean you caused the problem.

items.title: I know what you mean.
items.model: I know what you mean about the long commute.
examples: I know what you mean because I felt the same way.

items.title: That must have been [adjective].
items.model: That must have been exhausting after such a long flight.
examples: That must have been exciting for your whole family.

items.title: I can imagine.
items.cue: Show you can understand someone's experience.
items.model: I can imagine how frustrating that was.
examples: I can imagine why you needed a break.
items.meaning: Show you can understand someone's experience.

items.title: You must be [adjective].
items.cue: Make a sympathetic guess about a feeling.
items.model: You must be tired after the journey.
examples: You must be proud of your daughter.
items.meaning: Make a sympathetic guess about a feeling.

items.title: Good for you!
items.model: Good for you for trying something new!
examples: Good for you for asking for help!
items.note: Use a warm tone; a flat tone can sound sarcastic.

items.title: That's a relief.
items.model: That's a relief because I thought we'd missed it.
examples: That's a relief after all the trouble we had.

items.title: What a shame.
items.model: What a shame that the concert was cancelled.
examples: What a shame that you couldn't join us.

items.title: I hadn't thought of that.
items.model: I hadn't thought of that as an option.
examples: I hadn't thought of that before you mentioned it.

items.title: That's a good point.
items.model: That's a good point about the travel time.
examples: That's a good point, and we should check the cost.

items.title: I couldn't agree more.
items.model: I couldn't agree more about keeping things simple.
examples: I couldn't agree more with what you just said.

items.title: Not necessarily.
items.model: Not necessarily; the expensive one isn't always better.
examples: Not necessarily; some people prefer working alone.
items.note: Means not always true, rather than I do not know.

items.title: It depends on [factor].
items.cue: Say an answer changes with circumstances.
items.model: It depends on how much time we have.
examples: It depends on the weather tomorrow.
items.meaning: Say an answer changes with circumstances.

items.title: I suppose so.
items.model: I suppose so, although I'd like to check.
examples: I suppose so if everyone else is happy.
items.note: Less enthusiastic than Yes, definitely.

items.title: I wouldn't be surprised.
items.model: I wouldn't be surprised if the train is full.
examples: I wouldn't be surprised if she arrives early.

items.title: Tell me about it.
items.model: Tell me about it; my internet has been slow too.
examples: Tell me about it; I've also had a very long day.
items.note: Informal idiomatic agreement, usually not a literal request.

items.title: Could you say that again?
items.model: Could you say that again a little more slowly?
examples: Could you say that again so I can write it down?

items.title: Could you speak a little more slowly?
items.model: Could you speak a little more slowly, please?
examples: Could you speak a little more slowly while I take notes?
expressions: Could you speak a little more slowly?

items.title: What does [word] mean?
items.model: What does flexible mean in this advert?
examples: What does refundable mean on this ticket?

items.title: Do you mean [idea]?
items.model: Do you mean we should meet outside?
examples: Do you mean the price includes delivery?

items.title: Let me think for a moment.
items.model: Let me think for a moment before I answer.
examples: Let me think for a moment about the best route.
expressions: Let me think for a moment.

items.title: I didn't catch [part].
items.cue: Say what you did not hear.
items.model: I didn't catch the last part of your question.
examples: I didn't catch your name over the noise.
items.meaning: Say what you did not hear.

items.title: Could you spell that?
items.model: Could you spell that so I can search for it?
examples: Could you spell that name for me, please?

items.title: Could you give me an example?
items.model: Could you give me an example of what you mean?
examples: Could you give me an example from daily life?
expressions: Could you give me an example?

items.title: I'm not sure I understand.
items.cue: Say an explanation is still unclear.
items.model: I'm not sure I understand the second step.
examples: I'm not sure I understand what this button does.
items.meaning: Say an explanation is still unclear.

items.title: Let me check I've understood.
items.model: Let me check I've understood the instructions.
examples: Let me check I've understood what you need.

items.title: In other words, ...
items.model: In other words, we need to leave earlier.
examples: In other words, the first lesson is free.

items.title: What I mean is [idea].
items.model: What I mean is that I need more time.
examples: What I mean is that we can try a simpler version.

items.title: What I'm trying to say is [idea].
items.model: What I'm trying to say is that I felt left out.
examples: What I'm trying to say is that both options could work.
expressions: What I'm trying to say is [idea].

items.title: Let me put it another way.
items.model: Let me put it another way so it's clearer.
examples: Let me put it another way using a simple example.
expressions: Let me put it another way.

items.title: I've forgotten the word for it.
items.model: I've forgotten the word for it, but it opens bottles.
examples: I've forgotten the word for it, but you use it to weigh food.
expressions: I've forgotten the word for it.

items.title: It's a kind of [thing].
items.model: It's a kind of small electric oven.
examples: It's a kind of bag you wear around your waist.

items.title: It's used for [verb-ing].
items.model: It's used for measuring ingredients.
examples: It's used for keeping drinks cold.

items.title: How do you pronounce [word]?
items.cue: Ask how to say a word.
items.model: How do you pronounce comfortable?
examples: How do you pronounce this street name?
items.meaning: Ask how to say a word.

items.title: Did I say that correctly?
items.model: Did I say that correctly in the past tense?
examples: Did I say that correctly, or should I try again?

items.title: Let me start again.
items.model: Let me start again because I mixed up the dates.
examples: Let me start again and explain the main problem first.

items.title: Could you help me with [thing]?
items.model: Could you help me with this form?
examples: Could you help me with the shopping bags?

items.title: Could I have [thing], please?
items.model: Could I have a glass of water, please?
examples: Could I have a copy of the receipt, please?

items.title: Would you mind [verb-ing]?
items.model: Would you mind opening the window?
examples: Would you mind sending me the address?
items.note: Use -ing. No, not at all means the person agrees to help.

items.title: Is it okay if I [verb]?
items.model: Is it okay if I sit here?
examples: Is it okay if I call you tomorrow?

items.title: Can I borrow [thing]?
items.cue: Ask to use something and return it.
items.model: Can I borrow your pen for a minute?
examples: Can I borrow your charger until lunch?
items.meaning: Ask to use something and return it.
items.note: Borrow from someone; lend something to someone.

items.title: Could you give me a hand?
items.model: Could you give me a hand with this box?
examples: Could you give me a hand moving the table?
expressions: Could you give me a hand?
items.note: Friendly idiom for help.

items.title: Could you show me how to [verb]?
items.model: Could you show me how to use this machine?
examples: Could you show me how to get to the library?
expressions: Could you show me how to [verb]?

items.title: Would it be possible to [verb]?
items.model: Would it be possible to change my booking?
examples: Would it be possible to collect it tomorrow?

items.title: Could you do me a favour?
items.model: Could you do me a favour and check this message?
examples: Could you do me a favour and water my plants?
expressions: Could you do me a favour?

items.title: Do you happen to have [thing]?
items.cue: Ask gently whether something is available.
items.model: Do you happen to have a spare umbrella?
examples: Do you happen to have a pen I could use?
items.meaning: Ask gently whether something is available.

items.title: May I ask [question]?
items.model: May I ask what time you close?
examples: May I ask how much the repair will cost?
items.note: Slightly more formal than Can I ask.

items.title: Could I leave [thing] here?
items.model: Could I leave my bag here while I look around?
examples: Could I leave this parcel here until six?

items.title: Please let me know [information].
items.model: Please let me know when you arrive.
examples: Please let me know if the time changes.

items.title: I'd appreciate it if you could [verb].
items.cue: Make a polite, fairly formal request.
items.model: I'd appreciate it if you could reply by Friday.
examples: I'd appreciate it if you could check the figures.
expressions: I'd appreciate it if you could [verb].
items.meaning: Make a polite, fairly formal request.

items.title: There's no rush.
items.model: There's no rush, so take your time.
examples: There's no rush to send the photos today.

items.title: Whenever you have a moment, ...
items.model: Whenever you have a moment, could you check this?
examples: Whenever you have a moment, please call me back.

items.title: Let me know if you need a hand.
items.model: Let me know if you need a hand with dinner.
examples: Let me know if you need a hand carrying anything.
expressions: Let me know if you need a hand.

items.title: Shall I [verb]?
items.model: Shall I hold the door for you?
examples: Shall I bring some snacks?
items.note: Common in British English for offers and suggestions.

items.title: Would you like me to [verb]?
items.model: Would you like me to carry that?
examples: Would you like me to explain it again?

items.title: I'll take care of [thing].
items.model: I'll take care of the booking.
examples: I'll take care of the dishes tonight.

items.title: Are you free [time]?
items.model: Are you free on Saturday afternoon?
examples: Are you free for a quick call tomorrow?

items.title: Would you like to [verb]?
items.model: Would you like to join us for dinner?
examples: Would you like to go for a walk?

items.title: How about [verb-ing]?
items.model: How about meeting at the station?
examples: How about trying the new café?
items.note: Use a noun or -ing form after about.

items.title: That works for me.
items.model: That works for me, so I'll see you at seven.
examples: That works for me if we finish before lunch.

items.title: I'm looking forward to [thing].
items.cue: Express pleasure about a future event.
items.model: I'm looking forward to the weekend.
examples: I'm looking forward to seeing you again.
items.meaning: Express pleasure about a future event.
items.note: Use a noun or -ing form, not see after to.

items.title: Let's make a plan.
items.model: Let's make a plan for the school holidays.
examples: Let's make a plan before we book anything.

items.title: What time suits you?
items.model: What time suits you on Monday?
examples: What time suits you best for a call?

items.title: Where shall we meet?
items.model: Where shall we meet before the film?
examples: Where shall we meet after your class?

items.title: I'll check my calendar.
items.cue: Say you need to confirm availability.
items.model: I'll check my calendar and get back to you.
examples: I'll check my calendar before I say yes.
items.meaning: Say you need to confirm availability.

items.title: Can we move it to [time]?
items.model: Can we move it to Thursday morning?
examples: Can we move it to half past three?

items.title: Something has come up.
items.model: Something has come up, so I need to leave.
examples: Something has come up at work this afternoon.

items.title: I'm running a little late.
items.cue: Warn that you will arrive late.
items.model: I'm running a little late because of traffic.
examples: I'm running a little late, but I'm on my way.
items.meaning: Warn that you will arrive late.

items.title: I'll be there in [time].
items.model: I'll be there in about ten minutes.
examples: I'll be there in half an hour.

items.title: Let's play it by ear.
items.model: Let's play it by ear and see how we feel.
examples: Let's play it by ear if the weather changes.
items.note: Informal; avoid when someone needs a firm arrangement.

items.title: Let's keep in touch.
items.model: Let's keep in touch after the course.
examples: Let's keep in touch while you're away.

items.title: I'll let you know by [time].
items.cue: Promise a decision before a deadline.
items.model: I'll let you know by tomorrow evening.
examples: I'll let you know by Friday at the latest.
items.meaning: Promise a decision before a deadline.

items.title: Can I take a rain check?
items.cue: Decline now but suggest another occasion.
items.model: Can I take a rain check on dinner tonight?
examples: Can I take a rain check and join you next week?
expressions: Can I take a rain check?
items.meaning: Decline now but suggest another occasion.
items.note: Informal; implies interest in doing it another time.

items.title: I'd love to, but [reason].
items.model: I'd love to, but I already have plans.
examples: I'd love to, but I'm working that evening.

items.title: Maybe another time.
items.cue: Decline without fixing a new date.
items.model: Maybe another time, as I'm busy this weekend.
examples: Maybe another time when we both have a day off.
items.meaning: Decline without fixing a new date.
items.note: Softer with a thank-you; may not promise a future meeting.

items.title: It's a date.
items.model: It's a date; I'll meet you there on Friday.
examples: It's a date, and I'll book the table.
items.note: Informal; can be romantic or simply friendly depending on context.

items.title: wake up early
items.cue: Stop sleeping early in the day.
items.model: I wake up early on weekdays.
examples: I need to wake up early for my flight.
items.meaning: Stop sleeping early in the day.

items.title: get ready for [thing]
items.model: I get ready for work after breakfast.
examples: We need to get ready for the wedding.

items.title: have breakfast
items.cue: Eat the first meal of the day.
items.model: I have breakfast before checking my phone.
examples: We usually have breakfast together on Sundays.
items.meaning: Eat the first meal of the day.

items.title: head out
items.model: I need to head out in five minutes.
examples: We can head out after the rain stops.
items.note: Conversational.

items.title: get home
items.model: I usually get home around seven.
examples: Please call me when you get home.
items.note: Say get home, not get to home.

items.title: get out of bed
items.model: I find it hard to get out of bed on Mondays.
examples: I got out of bed when the alarm rang.

items.title: hit the snooze button
items.model: I hit the snooze button twice this morning.
examples: I try not to hit the snooze button anymore.
items.note: Informal daily-life expression.

items.title: brush my teeth
items.cue: Clean your teeth with a toothbrush.
items.model: I brush my teeth before I leave.
examples: I forgot to brush my teeth before breakfast.
items.meaning: Clean your teeth with a toothbrush.

items.title: take a shower
items.model: I take a shower after exercising.
examples: I'll take a shower before dinner.
items.note: Have a shower is also common, especially in British English.

items.title: get dressed
items.model: I get dressed before making coffee.
examples: The children need to get dressed for school.

items.title: make the bed
items.model: I make the bed every morning.
examples: Could you make the bed while I open the curtains?

items.title: pack my bag
items.cue: Put necessary items in a bag.
items.model: I pack my bag the night before.
examples: I need to pack my bag for the gym.
items.meaning: Put necessary items in a bag.

items.title: grab a quick bite
items.model: I'll grab a quick bite before the meeting.
examples: We can grab a quick bite at the station.
items.note: Informal.

items.title: leave for [place]
items.model: I leave for work at eight.
examples: We should leave for the airport soon.

items.title: take a short break
items.model: Let's take a short break before continuing.
examples: I take a short break after each study session.

items.title: wind down
items.model: I read a book to wind down at night.
examples: It takes me a while to wind down after work.

items.title: set an alarm
items.cue: Choose a time for an alarm.
items.model: I'll set an alarm for six tomorrow.
examples: Remember to set an alarm before you sleep.
items.meaning: Choose a time for an alarm.

items.title: get an early night
items.cue: Go to bed earlier than usual.
items.model: I need to get an early night before the trip.
examples: Let's get an early night after such a busy day.
items.meaning: Go to bed earlier than usual.
items.note: Common in British English.

items.title: stay up late
items.model: I sometimes stay up late watching films.
examples: I don't want to stay up late tonight.

items.title: get enough sleep
items.cue: Sleep for a sufficient amount of time.
items.model: I feel better when I get enough sleep.
examples: It's difficult to get enough sleep during a busy week.
items.meaning: Sleep for a sufficient amount of time.

items.title: do the laundry
items.model: I do the laundry on Saturday mornings.
examples: Could you do the laundry while I buy groceries?

items.title: wash the dishes
items.model: I'll wash the dishes after dinner.
examples: We take turns washing the dishes.

items.title: take out the rubbish
items.model: Please take out the rubbish before you leave.
examples: I forgot to take out the rubbish last night.
items.note: British wording; take out the trash is common in American English.

items.title: tidy up
items.model: Let's tidy up before our guests arrive.
examples: I need to tidy up my desk.

items.title: run out of [thing]
items.model: We've run out of milk.
examples: I always run out of clean socks on Fridays.

items.title: put [thing] away
items.cue: Return something to its proper place.
items.model: Please put your shoes away.
examples: I'll put the dishes away when they're dry.
items.meaning: Return something to its proper place.
items.note: With a pronoun, say put it away, not put away it.

items.title: hang up the washing
items.cue: Put washed clothes up to dry.
items.model: I'll hang up the washing outside.
examples: Could you hang up the washing before it gets dark?
items.meaning: Put washed clothes up to dry.

items.title: wipe down [surface]
items.cue: Clean a surface with a cloth.
items.model: Please wipe down the table after lunch.
examples: I wipe down the kitchen counter every evening.
items.meaning: Clean a surface with a cloth.

items.title: sweep the floor
items.cue: Clean the floor with a broom.
items.model: I'll sweep the floor before I mop it.
examples: We need to sweep the floor after the party.
items.meaning: Clean the floor with a broom.

items.title: change the sheets
items.cue: Put clean bed linen on a bed.
items.model: I change the sheets every weekend.
examples: Could you change the sheets in the guest room?
items.meaning: Put clean bed linen on a bed.

items.title: water the plants
items.model: Please water the plants while I'm away.
examples: I water the plants before the sun gets too hot.

items.title: turn off [device]
items.cue: Stop a device or light working.
items.model: Please turn off the lights before leaving.
examples: I always turn off the fan at night.
items.meaning: Stop a device or light working.
items.note: With a pronoun, use turn it off.

items.title: plug in [device]
items.model: I need to plug in my laptop.
examples: Could you plug in the kettle for me?
items.note: With a pronoun, use plug it in.

items.title: The [thing] isn't working.
items.model: The washing machine isn't working this morning.
examples: The doorbell isn't working, so please call me.

items.title: There's a leak in [place].
items.cue: Report escaping water or another fluid.
items.model: There's a leak in the bathroom pipe.
examples: There's a leak in the roof above the kitchen.
items.meaning: Report escaping water or another fluid.

items.title: The drain is blocked.
items.cue: Report water that cannot flow away.
items.model: The drain is blocked in the bathroom.
examples: The drain is blocked, so the sink fills up.
items.meaning: Report water that cannot flow away.

items.title: Could you send someone to fix it?
items.model: Could you send someone to fix it this week?
examples: Could you send someone to fix it before Friday?
expressions: Could you send someone to fix it?

items.title: When will it be ready?
items.cue: Ask when a task will be finished.
items.model: When will it be ready for collection?
examples: When will it be ready for us to use again?
items.meaning: Ask when a task will be finished.

items.title: keep the noise down
items.model: Could you keep the noise down after ten?
examples: We try to keep the noise down in the evenings.

items.title: lock myself out
items.cue: Accidentally leave myself unable to enter.
items.model: I don't want to lock myself out again.
examples: I managed to lock myself out while taking out the bins.
items.meaning: Accidentally leave myself unable to enter.
items.note: Change myself to yourself/himself etc. as needed.

items.title: make a shopping list
items.model: I make a shopping list before going out.
examples: Let's make a shopping list for the week.

items.title: pick up some [food]
items.cue: Buy food while you are out.
items.model: Could you pick up some bread on your way home?
examples: I'll pick up some fruit after work.
items.meaning: Buy food while you are out.

items.title: What do we need?
items.model: What do we need for dinner tonight?
examples: What do we need from the supermarket?

items.title: How much [food] do we have?
items.cue: Ask the amount of an uncountable food.
items.model: How much rice do we have left?
examples: How much milk do we have in the fridge?
items.meaning: Ask the amount of an uncountable food.
items.note: Use How many for countable items, such as eggs.

items.title: put the kettle on
items.cue: Start heating water in a kettle.
items.model: I'll put the kettle on for tea.
examples: Could you put the kettle on while I find some cups?
items.meaning: Start heating water in a kettle.

items.title: chop the vegetables
items.model: I'll chop the vegetables while you cook the rice.
examples: We need to chop the vegetables for the soup.

items.title: heat up [food]
items.model: I'll heat up the soup for lunch.
examples: Can you heat up the leftovers?
items.note: With a pronoun, use heat it up.

items.title: bring [liquid] to the boil
items.model: Bring the water to the boil before adding the pasta.
examples: Bring the soup to the boil, then lower the heat.

items.title: turn down the heat
items.model: Turn down the heat so the sauce doesn't burn.
examples: I'll turn down the heat once the water boils.

items.title: stir in [ingredient]
items.cue: Mix an ingredient into food by stirring.
items.model: Stir in the milk slowly.
examples: I'll stir in the cheese just before serving.
items.meaning: Mix an ingredient into food by stirring.

items.title: add a pinch of [ingredient]
items.model: Add a pinch of salt to the soup.
examples: I usually add a pinch of cinnamon to my oats.

items.title: season to taste
items.cue: Add seasoning until the flavour suits you.
items.model: Season to taste before serving the soup.
examples: I season to taste after the vegetables are cooked.
items.meaning: Add seasoning until the flavour suits you.

items.title: leave it to cool
items.cue: Wait for something to become cooler.
items.model: Leave it to cool before putting it in the fridge.
examples: We should leave it to cool before cutting it.
items.meaning: Wait for something to become cooler.

items.title: keep it in the fridge
items.model: Keep it in the fridge until dinner.
examples: Please keep it in the fridge once it's opened.

items.title: use up [food]
items.model: We should use up these tomatoes today.
examples: I'll use up the rice in a fried rice dish.
items.note: With a pronoun, use use it up.

items.title: go off
items.cue: Become no longer fresh or safe to eat.
items.model: Milk can go off if it's left outside.
examples: These strawberries will go off if we keep them too long.
items.meaning: Become no longer fresh or safe to eat.
items.note: British food usage; spoil is common in American English.

items.title: be on special offer
items.cue: Be sold at a reduced price.
items.model: These apples are on special offer today.
examples: The cereal was on special offer last week.
items.meaning: Be sold at a reduced price.

items.title: buy in bulk
items.cue: Buy a large quantity at once.
items.model: We buy rice in bulk to save money.
examples: I don't buy vegetables in bulk because we waste them.
items.meaning: Buy a large quantity at once.

items.title: Where can I find [item]?
items.model: Where can I find the cooking oil?
examples: Where can I find gluten-free bread?

items.title: Do you have any [item] left?
items.cue: Ask whether an item is still available.
items.model: Do you have any fresh eggs left?
examples: Do you have any small bags of rice left?
items.meaning: Ask whether an item is still available.

items.title: A table for [number], please.
items.model: Could we have a table for two, please?
examples: I'd like a table for four, please.

items.title: Could we see the menu?
items.cue: Ask for the list of dishes.
items.model: Could we see the menu before ordering drinks?
examples: Could we see the menu for breakfast?
items.meaning: Ask for the list of dishes.

items.title: I'd like [food], please.
items.model: I'd like the chicken rice, please.
examples: I'd like a small iced coffee, please.

items.title: Could we have the bill, please?
items.cue: Ask to pay after a meal.
items.model: Could we have the bill, please, when you have a moment?
examples: Could we have the bill, please, as we need to leave?
expressions: Could we have the bill, please?
items.meaning: Ask to pay after a meal.
items.note: Bill is British usage; check is common in the US.

items.title: Is this for here or to go?
items.cue: Ask whether food will be eaten on site.
items.model: Is this for here or to go today?
examples: Is this for here or to go, and would you like a bag?
expressions: Is this for here or to go?
items.meaning: Ask whether food will be eaten on site.
items.note: Common service question, especially in North America; eat in or take away in British English.

items.title: I have a reservation under [name].
items.model: I have a reservation under Tan for seven o'clock.
examples: I have a reservation under Aisha for four people.

items.title: Could we sit outside?
items.model: Could we sit outside if there's a table free?
examples: Could we sit outside near the entrance?

items.title: What would you recommend?
items.model: What would you recommend for someone who likes spicy food?
examples: What would you recommend from the lunch menu?

items.title: What comes with [dish]?
items.model: What comes with the grilled fish?
examples: What comes with the breakfast set?

items.title: Does this contain [ingredient]?
items.model: Does this contain any peanuts?
examples: Does this contain milk or cream?

items.title: I'm allergic to [ingredient].
items.cue: Tell staff about a food allergy.
items.model: I'm allergic to peanuts, so please check with the kitchen.
examples: I'm allergic to shellfish; can this be prepared safely?
items.meaning: Tell staff about a food allergy.
items.note: Use only for an actual allergy; clearly state it rather than saying dislike.

items.title: Could I have it without [ingredient]?
items.cue: Request that an ingredient be omitted.
items.model: Could I have it without onions?
examples: Could I have it without the sauce?
items.meaning: Request that an ingredient be omitted.

items.title: Could you make it less spicy?
items.cue: Ask for less heat in a dish.
items.model: Could you make it less spicy for me, please?
examples: Could you make it less spicy than the usual version?
expressions: Could you make it less spicy?
items.meaning: Ask for less heat in a dish.

items.title: Could I have the dressing on the side?
items.model: Could I have the dressing on the side, please?
examples: Could I have the dressing on the side with this salad?
expressions: Could I have the dressing on the side?

items.title: I'm still deciding.
items.cue: Ask for more time to choose.
items.model: I'm still deciding, so could you give me a minute?
examples: I'm still deciding between the noodles and the rice.
items.meaning: Ask for more time to choose.

items.title: That's all for now.
items.cue: Finish an order for the moment.
items.model: That's all for now, but we may order dessert later.
examples: That's all for now, thank you.
items.meaning: Finish an order for the moment.

items.title: I think there's been a mistake.
items.model: I think there's been a mistake with our order.
examples: I think there's been a mistake on the bill.
expressions: I think there's been a mistake.

items.title: We ordered [item].
items.model: We ordered two coffees, but only one arrived.
examples: We ordered the vegetarian noodles.

items.title: Could we pay separately?
items.model: Could we pay separately for our meals?
examples: Could we pay separately by card?

items.title: Could I get this to take away?
items.cue: Ask to take food with you.
items.model: Could I get this to take away instead?
examples: Could I get this to take away in a small box?
expressions: Could I get this to take away?
items.meaning: Ask to take food with you.

items.title: I'm just looking, thanks.
items.model: I'm just looking, thanks, but I'll ask if I need help.
examples: I'm just looking, thanks; I haven't decided yet.

items.title: How much is [item]?
items.model: How much is this jacket?
examples: How much is the blue bag in the window?

items.title: Do you have this in [size/colour]?
items.model: Do you have this in a medium?
examples: Do you have this in dark green?

items.title: Can I try this on?
items.cue: Ask to check how clothing fits.
items.model: Can I try this on before I buy it?
examples: Can I try this on in the fitting room?
items.meaning: Ask to check how clothing fits.

items.title: I'd like to return [item].
items.cue: Ask to give a purchase back.
items.model: I'd like to return this shirt because it doesn't fit.
examples: I'd like to return these headphones because they're faulty.
items.meaning: Ask to give a purchase back.

items.title: It doesn't fit.
items.cue: Say clothing is the wrong size or shape.
items.model: It doesn't fit around the shoulders.
examples: It doesn't fit, so I'll try a larger size.
items.meaning: Say clothing is the wrong size or shape.

items.title: It's a bit too [adjective].
items.model: It's a bit too tight around the waist.
examples: It's a bit too expensive for me.

items.title: It suits you.
items.cue: Say something looks good on a person.
items.model: It suits you because the colour brings out your eyes.
examples: It suits you better than the grey one.
items.meaning: Say something looks good on a person.
items.note: Suit concerns appearance; fit concerns size and shape.

items.title: I'm looking for [item].
items.cue: Tell an assistant what you want.
items.model: I'm looking for a pair of comfortable shoes.
examples: I'm looking for a gift for my sister.
items.meaning: Tell an assistant what you want.

items.title: What's the difference between [A] and [B]?
items.model: What's the difference between these two models?
examples: What's the difference between the standard and premium versions?

items.title: Is this on sale?
items.cue: Ask whether the price is reduced.
items.model: Is this on sale this week?
examples: Is this on sale, or is that the regular price?
items.meaning: Ask whether the price is reduced.

items.title: Does the price include [thing]?
items.model: Does the price include delivery?
examples: Does the price include installation?

items.title: I'll take it.
items.model: I'll take it if it comes with a receipt.
examples: I'll take it in black, please.

items.title: I'll think about it.
items.model: I'll think about it and come back tomorrow.
examples: I'll think about it before spending that much.

items.title: Do you accept cards?
items.model: Do you accept cards for small purchases?
examples: Do you accept cards, or is it cash only?

items.title: Could I have a receipt?
items.model: Could I have a receipt for this purchase?
examples: Could I have a receipt by email?

items.title: Can I exchange it for [item]?
items.model: Can I exchange it for a larger size?
examples: Can I exchange it for the same model in blue?

items.title: Is there a warranty?
items.model: Is there a warranty on this appliance?
examples: Is there a warranty that covers repairs?

items.title: It's out of stock.
items.model: It's out of stock at this branch.
examples: It's out of stock, but we can order it for you.

items.title: When will you get more in?
items.model: When will you get more in this size?
examples: When will you get more in at this branch?
expressions: When will you get more in?

items.title: stick to a budget
items.model: I'm trying to stick to a budget this month.
examples: We need to stick to a budget for the trip.

items.title: save up for [thing]
items.cue: Gradually keep money for a purchase.
items.model: I'm saving up for a new laptop.
examples: We're saving up for a family holiday.
items.meaning: Gradually keep money for a purchase.

items.title: split the bill
items.model: Let's split the bill equally.
examples: Would you like to split the bill?

items.title: pay by card
items.cue: Use a bank card to pay.
items.model: Can I pay by card here?
examples: I usually pay by card at the supermarket.
items.meaning: Use a bank card to pay.

items.title: How much do I owe you?
items.model: How much do I owe you for lunch?
examples: How much do I owe you for the tickets?
expressions: How much do I owe you?

items.title: be short of cash
items.model: I'm a little short of cash this week.
examples: We were short of cash after paying the deposit.

items.title: set some money aside
items.model: I set some money aside each month.
examples: Let's set some money aside for repairs.

items.title: cut back on [spending]
items.model: I'm cutting back on takeaway meals.
examples: We need to cut back on unnecessary subscriptions.

items.title: be worth the money
items.cue: Give enough value for the price.
items.model: These shoes are worth the money because they last.
examples: I don't think the upgrade is worth the money.
items.meaning: Give enough value for the price.

items.title: be within my budget
items.cue: Cost an affordable amount for my plan.
items.model: This room is within my budget.
examples: I need something that's within my budget.
items.meaning: Cost an affordable amount for my plan.

items.title: be more than I can afford
items.model: That flat is more than I can afford.
examples: A new car is more than I can afford right now.
expressions: be more than I can afford

items.title: Could you break this note?
items.model: Could you break this note into smaller notes?
examples: Could you break this note so I can pay for parking?
items.note: Usage varies by country; in the US, break this bill is common.

items.title: keep the change
items.cue: Tell someone not to return the extra money.
items.model: You can keep the change.
examples: Please keep the change as a tip.
items.meaning: Tell someone not to return the extra money.

items.title: transfer the money
items.model: I'll transfer the money after lunch.
examples: Could you transfer the money to my account today?

items.title: The payment didn't go through.
items.model: The payment didn't go through on my first attempt.
examples: The payment didn't go through, so I'll check my bank app.

items.title: I've been charged twice.
items.model: I've been charged twice for the same order.
examples: I've been charged twice, but I only bought one ticket.

items.title: When is the payment due?
items.model: When is the payment due for this course?
examples: When is the payment due on the electricity bill?

items.title: pay in instalments
items.model: Can I pay in instalments for this course?
examples: We decided to pay in instalments over three months.

items.title: Is there an extra charge?
items.model: Is there an extra charge for delivery?
examples: Is there an extra charge if we arrive late?

items.title: Could you check the amount?
items.cue: Ask someone to verify a total.
items.model: Could you check the amount on this receipt?
examples: Could you check the amount before I pay?
items.meaning: Ask someone to verify a total.

items.title: How do I get to [place]?
items.model: How do I get to the nearest train station?
examples: How do I get to the museum from here?

items.title: Is it within walking distance?
items.model: Is it within walking distance of the hotel?
examples: Is it within walking distance, or should we take a bus?

items.title: go straight ahead
items.model: Go straight ahead until you reach the traffic lights.
examples: You need to go straight ahead past the bank.

items.title: turn left at [place]
items.model: Turn left at the next junction.
examples: You should turn left at the pharmacy.

items.title: turn right at [place]
items.model: Turn right at the end of this road.
examples: You need to turn right at the second traffic light.

items.title: It's on your left.
items.cue: Locate something to the left of the listener.
items.model: It's on your left, just after the bakery.
examples: It's on your left when you come out of the lift.
items.meaning: Locate something to the left of the listener.

items.title: It's across from [place].
items.cue: Locate something on the opposite side.
items.model: It's across from the post office.
examples: It's across from the main entrance to the park.
items.meaning: Locate something on the opposite side.

items.title: It's next to [place].
items.cue: Locate something immediately beside another place.
items.model: It's next to the supermarket.
examples: It's next to the lift on the third floor.
items.meaning: Locate something immediately beside another place.

items.title: I'm on my way.
items.model: I'm on my way and should arrive soon.
examples: I'm on my way to the station now.

items.title: I'm stuck in traffic.
items.model: I'm stuck in traffic near the bridge.
examples: I'm stuck in traffic, so please start without me.

items.title: Could you drop me off at [place]?
items.cue: Ask to leave a vehicle at a place.
items.model: Could you drop me off at the main entrance?
examples: Could you drop me off at the station?
expressions: Could you drop me off at [place]?
items.meaning: Ask to leave a vehicle at a place.

items.title: Could you pick me up from [place]?
items.model: Could you pick me up from the airport?
examples: Could you pick me up from work at six?
expressions: Could you pick me up from [place]?

items.title: Which platform does it leave from?
items.cue: Ask where to board a train.
items.model: Which platform does it leave from today?
examples: Which platform does it leave from for Ipoh?
expressions: Which platform does it leave from?
items.meaning: Ask where to board a train.

items.title: Does this bus go to [place]?
items.model: Does this bus go to the city centre?
examples: Does this bus go to the hospital?

items.title: Where should I get off?
items.cue: Ask which stop to leave at.
items.model: Where should I get off for the library?
examples: Where should I get off if I want the market?
items.meaning: Ask which stop to leave at.

items.title: How long does it take?
items.model: How long does it take to walk there?
examples: How long does it take during rush hour?

items.title: I think we're going the wrong way.
items.model: I think we're going the wrong way because the river is behind us.
examples: I think we're going the wrong way, so let's check the map.
expressions: I think we're going the wrong way.

items.title: Is there a faster way?
items.model: Is there a faster way to reach the airport?
examples: Is there a faster way that avoids the traffic?

items.title: Where can I park?
items.model: Where can I park near the building?
examples: Where can I park without blocking the entrance?

items.title: Could you wait here for a moment?
items.model: Could you wait here for a moment while I get my bag?
examples: Could you wait here for a moment until my friend arrives?
expressions: Could you wait here for a moment?

items.title: I'd like to check in.
items.cue: Start a hotel or flight check-in.
items.model: I'd like to check in for my flight to Singapore.
examples: I'd like to check in under the name Lee.
items.meaning: Start a hotel or flight check-in.

items.title: I have a booking under [name].
items.model: I have a booking under Wong for two nights.
examples: I have a booking under Priya for a double room.

items.title: What time is check-out?
items.cue: Ask when you must leave a hotel room.
items.model: What time is check-out tomorrow?
examples: What time is check-out on Sunday?
items.meaning: Ask when you must leave a hotel room.

items.title: Is breakfast included?
items.model: Is breakfast included in the room price?
examples: Is breakfast included with this booking?

items.title: Could I leave my luggage here?
items.cue: Ask a hotel to store bags.
items.model: Could I leave my luggage here until my flight?
examples: Could I leave my luggage here before check-in?
expressions: Could I leave my luggage here?
items.meaning: Ask a hotel to store bags.

items.title: Where is the boarding gate?
items.cue: Ask where to board a plane.
items.model: Where is the boarding gate for this flight?
examples: Where is the boarding gate shown on my pass?
items.meaning: Ask where to board a plane.

items.title: Has the flight been delayed?
items.model: Has the flight been delayed again?
examples: Has the flight been delayed because of the weather?

items.title: Is this the queue for [thing]?
items.cue: Check that you are waiting in the right line.
items.model: Is this the queue for baggage drop?
examples: Is this the queue for passport control?
items.meaning: Check that you are waiting in the right line.

items.title: I have a connecting flight.
items.cue: Explain that you must catch another plane.
items.model: I have a connecting flight in two hours.
examples: I have a connecting flight, so where should I go next?
items.meaning: Explain that you must catch another plane.

items.title: My luggage hasn't arrived.
items.model: My luggage hasn't arrived on the belt.
examples: My luggage hasn't arrived, and I need to report it.

items.title: Where can I collect [thing]?
items.cue: Ask where to retrieve an item.
items.model: Where can I collect my checked luggage?
examples: Where can I collect my train tickets?
items.meaning: Ask where to retrieve an item.

items.title: Could I have a window seat?
items.cue: Request a seat beside the window.
items.model: Could I have a window seat if one is available?
examples: Could I have a window seat on the return flight?
expressions: Could I have a window seat?
items.meaning: Request a seat beside the window.

items.title: I'd prefer an aisle seat.
items.model: I'd prefer an aisle seat near the front.
examples: I'd prefer an aisle seat so I can get up easily.

items.title: How do I connect to the Wi-Fi?
items.cue: Ask how to access the internet.
items.model: How do I connect to the Wi-Fi in my room?
examples: How do I connect to the Wi-Fi at the airport?
expressions: How do I connect to the Wi-Fi?
items.meaning: Ask how to access the internet.

items.title: Could I get an extra [item]?
items.model: Could I get an extra towel, please?
examples: Could I get an extra pillow for the room?

items.title: The room hasn't been cleaned.
items.model: The room hasn't been cleaned since we arrived.
examples: The room hasn't been cleaned, and the towels are used.

items.title: Could we change rooms?
items.cue: Ask for a different hotel room.
items.model: Could we change rooms because it's very noisy?
examples: Could we change rooms to one away from the lift?
items.meaning: Ask for a different hotel room.

items.title: Is there a shuttle service?
items.model: Is there a shuttle service to the airport?
examples: Is there a shuttle service from the station?

items.title: I'd like to extend my stay.
items.cue: Ask to remain at accommodation longer.
items.model: I'd like to extend my stay by one night.
examples: I'd like to extend my stay until Monday.
expressions: I'd like to extend my stay.
items.meaning: Ask to remain at accommodation longer.

items.title: Can I cancel without a fee?
items.model: Can I cancel without a fee before Friday?
examples: Can I cancel without a fee if my flight changes?
expressions: Can I cancel without a fee?

items.title: I'd like to make an appointment.
items.model: I'd like to make an appointment with the dentist.
examples: I'd like to make an appointment for tomorrow afternoon.
expressions: I'd like to make an appointment.

items.title: I'm not feeling well.
items.model: I'm not feeling well, so I'll stay home.
examples: I'm not feeling well enough to go to work.

items.title: I have a [symptom].
items.model: I have a headache that started this morning.
examples: I have a sore throat and a cough.
items.note: Use I have a fever/cough, but I have diarrhoea without a.

items.title: It hurts when I [verb].
items.model: It hurts when I swallow.
examples: It hurts when I bend my knee.

items.title: I need help right away.
items.model: I need help right away because someone has collapsed.
examples: I need help right away at the main entrance.

items.title: I've been feeling [adjective].
items.model: I've been feeling dizzy since this morning.
examples: I've been feeling unusually tired this week.

items.title: It started [time].
items.model: It started yesterday after dinner.
examples: It started about an hour ago.

items.title: The pain is in my [body part].
items.model: The pain is in my lower back.
examples: The pain is in my left shoulder.
expressions: The pain is in my [body part].

items.title: I'm taking [medicine].
items.model: I'm taking medicine for my blood pressure.
examples: I'm taking an antibiotic prescribed yesterday.
items.note: Practise with your actual medicine name when speaking to a clinician.

items.title: I'm allergic to this medicine.
items.model: I'm allergic to this medicine and need an alternative.
examples: I'm allergic to this medicine; it's listed in my records.

items.title: Do I need a prescription?
items.cue: Ask if medical authorisation is required.
items.model: Do I need a prescription for this medicine?
examples: Do I need a prescription before ordering it?
items.meaning: Ask if medical authorisation is required.

items.title: How often should I take it?
items.model: How often should I take it each day?
examples: How often should I take it after the first week?
expressions: How often should I take it?

items.model: If I were you, I'd ask for more details.
examples: If I were you, I'd try the smaller size.
items.meaning: Offer advice from another person's position.
items.note: I'd means I would here; use advice thoughtfully.

items.title: The more I [verb], the more [result].
items.model: The more I practise, the more confident I feel.
examples: The more I read, the more useful phrases I notice.

items.title: It's worth [verb-ing].
items.cue: Say an action deserves the effort.
items.model: It's worth checking the price online.
examples: It's worth practising this before your appointment.
items.meaning: Say an action deserves the effort.
items.note: Use -ing, not to check.

items.title: There's no need to [verb].
items.model: There's no need to rush.
examples: There's no need to apologise for asking a question.
